primitives.note: Basic attacks consume up to 2 shells, then reload; reload duration shortens with bonus attack speed and level, non-monotonically (worse between 150%-200% bonus AS).

Each basic attack fires 4 pellets (6 on crit), each a separate physical damage instance; only the first pellet applies on-hit/lifesteal and takes the full ratio, later pellets deal ~0.333x that ratio.
Critical strikes change pellet count from 4 to 6 and apply a special per-pellet crit-damage multiplier rather than standard crit doubling.
Quickdraw resets Graves' basic attack timer on cast; other resets do not.
Quickdraw's current cooldown is reduced 0.5s per pellet that lands on an enemy, letting it be recast (and attack-reset) more often.
True Grit: stacks (cap 8, 4s duration each) grant bonus armor and MR; relevant to Graves' damage taken in the survival fight.
Q initial hit, W impact, and R shell/explosion each deal damage on cast or fixed delay, on cooldown.
Q has two separately timed damage parts (initial pass, then trail detonation ~2s later); R has a shell-hit part and a separate cone-explosion part.
Mana costs (80/70-90/40/100) across four abilities materially cap how many casts fit in a 15s dummy fight.
Q's trail detonation is a wide perpendicular area and R's explosion is an anchored cone; against a single stationary dummy this collapses to a simple 'does it also hit the same target' assumption.

needsBespoke.why: Two pieces of Graves' passive are not expressible as plain instantiations of the primitives: (1) the base per-pellet AD ratio is computed in the bin via an unresolved ByCharLevelFormulaCalculationPart, so the exact numeric level curve must be taken from the wiki's formula rather than the bin, and (2) the shell reload timer's dependence on bonus attack speed is explicitly nonlinear and non-monotonic (worse between 150%-200% bonus AS, 'confirmed to be confusing' per the wiki itself), which the generic weapon-or-ammo-system primitive cannot correctly express without a bespoke reload-speed curve.

unsettled.question: What is the exact numeric per-level AD ratio for a single pellet's base damage, given the bin's calculation part is unresolved?
options: Use the wiki's explicit per-level formula: 100*(0.6895 + 0.01765*x*(0.595 + 0.0225*(x-1)))% AD
Treat the bin's unresolved ByCharLevelFormulaCalculationPart as authoritative and flag as unknown until resolved

unsettled.question: How exactly does Graves' shell reload speed scale with bonus attack speed inside the simulator, given the wiki states the precise formula is unknown and behaves non-monotonically between 150% and 200% bonus AS?
options: Model reload speed as directly tied to total attack speed via the capped formula implied by the notes (max reload speed pplevel curve)
Approximate reload time as the flat base values (2.08s/1.3s) unaffected by attack speed for simplicity
Model reload speed scaling linearly with bonus AS up to 150% only, ignoring the confusing 150-200% band
quotes: Precise formula is unknown, but it is confirmed to be confusing.
Values of {{as|'''bonus''' attack speed}} between {{as|150%|attack speed}} and {{as|200%|attack speed}} have a negative effect on '''Graves' ''' reload speed.

unsettled.question: Against a single stationary dummy, does R's cone explosion also hit the same target that was already hit by the initial shell, or is the cone damage only for 'additional' enemies distinct from the one hit by the shell?
options: The dummy takes both the initial shell damage (r_1) and the cone explosion damage (r_2) since it is the only target present
The dummy only takes the initial shell damage (r_1); the cone explosion is defined as hitting 'additional enemies' and does not re-hit the champion already struck
quotes: Upon hitting an enemy {{tip|champion}} or reaching the end of its range, the shell explodes in a cone to deal reduced damage to additional enemies.

proposal: Open with Q (End of the Line) on the dummy for its initial pass damage, then let the trail detonate ~2 seconds later for the second damage instance.
Auto-attack continuously whenever not casting, letting pellets land and cycling through the 2-shell magazine with its reload downtime.
Cast R (Collateral Damage) as soon as it is off cooldown for its large upfront physical damage.
Cast W (Smoke Screen) on the dummy when off cooldown and mana allows, for its magic damage impact.

Use E (Quickdraw) mainly to reset the basic attack timer and reduce its own cooldown from landed pellets, timing it to weave in extra attacks rather than for its own damage (Quickdraw itself deals none).
Re-cast Q on cooldown throughout the fight; if mana runs low, prioritize Q and basic attacks over W since Q has the shortest cooldown and strong AD scaling relative to cost.
Continue this Q/R/W/basic-attack cycle for the full ~15 seconds, keeping the shell magazine and mana pool as full as possible between casts.
questions: Does the simulator model Graves' reload timer and its interaction with attack speed precisely enough to know his true attack cadence, or should reload be simplified to a fixed value for this fight?

Is it worth spending mana on E (Quickdraw) purely for the attack-reset and self cooldown-reduction benefit, or should E be skipped entirely in a pure damage-maximization rotation since it deals no direct damage?

At the assumed level/items for the damage fight, does Graves have enough mana to cast Q, W, and R on cooldown for the full 15 seconds, or does a resource shortfall force cutting W or E from the rotation?

For R, should the dummy be assumed positioned to take only the initial shell hit, only the cone explosion, or both, and does that change which rotation order (e.g., casting R at range vs. point-blank) is 'optimal'?
